name: Stat Engine API
description:
Normalized, source-agnostic sports data API. Major competition coverage includes NBA, MLB, NFL, NHL, KBO, NCAA (basketball and football), and soccer competitions such as EPL, La Liga, Bundesliga, Serie A, Ligue 1, UCL, MLS, and FIFA tournaments.

The complete canonical sport identifiers understood by the API are: `basketball`, `football`, `baseball`, `hockey`, `soccer`, `golf`, `tennis`, `racing`, `mma`, `lacrosse`, `rugby`, `volleyball`, `australian_football`, `rugby_league`, `water_polo`, and `field_hockey`. These identifiers describe data shape; call `GET /v1/competitions` for the currently registered competition slugs and `GET /v1/competitions/{comp}/capabilities` for the phases, measures, and standings tables available for a particular competition.

Core resources — persons, teams, competitions/editions, contests, and entrants — carry minted ids that serialize as `<prefix>_<base32>` (`per_`, `team_`, `comp_`, `edt_`, `game_`, `cst_`, `ent_`); the prefix is part of the type. Stats are typed per-phase and reconstruct as-of any ingested instant from appearance facts.

## Endpoint groups

| Group | Base path | Description |
|-------|-----------|-------------|
| Persons | `/v1/persons` | Profile, appearances, game log, memberships, season stats, per-person capability discovery, composed player overview |
| Teams | `/v1/teams` | Profile, as-of roster, games, game log, season stats |
| Competitions | `/v1/competitions` | Competitions, editions, edition participants/games/standings, capability discovery |
| Contests | `/v1/contests` | Generalized contest detail for team matches, individual matches, and field/N-ary events; team-match boxscores and sport-scoped play-by-play where available |
| Analysis | `/v1/analysis` | Player-prop card and team comparison (all plans; metered at analysis weights) |
| Account | `/v1/account` | Authenticated plan usage (unmetered — checking quota never consumes units) |
| Assets | `/v1/assets` | Team logo PNGs (proxied, 7-day cache) |

## Authentication

All endpoints in this spec require an API key passed in the `X-API-Key` request header.

## Operational endpoints

Liveness/readiness probes (`/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/metrics`) and ingest administration endpoints (`/v1/ingest/...`) are intentionally **not documented in this spec**. They are operator-only surfaces and live in a separate internal spec; see infra docs for access.

## Response envelope

Every response wraps its payload in:

```json
{
  "data": {... },
  "meta": {
    "request_id": "uuid",
    "source": "source identifier",
    "fetched_at": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "cache": "HIT | MISS | STALE",
    "version": "v1"
  }
}
```

Error responses use `{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "..." } }`.
`meta.request_id` uniquely identifies the request — quote it when filing support tickets. `meta.cache` is reserved for response-layer caching (`HIT` / `STALE` / `MISS`); entity reads are currently served directly from the canonical store and always report `MISS`.

## Freshness

Reads are served from the canonical store, which ingest refreshes out-of-band on a per-resource cadence:

- **Live box scores** are re-ingested within minutes of in-game updates while a slate is live.
- **Standings** are recomputed whenever a game in the edition finalizes.
- **Schedules** are re-synced several times per day.
- **Final box scores** are immutable once a game is final.

`meta.fetched_at` reports when the response was assembled, not when the underlying data last changed upstream.

## Capability discovery

Call `GET /v1/competitions/{comp}/capabilities` to retrieve the exact stat keys (base + derived measures) each phase reports for a competition's sport.

Call `GET /v1/persons/{person_id}/capabilities?competition=&season=` to retrieve only the phases (and their stat keys) a specific person **actually recorded data for** that season — a presence-filtered projection of the same registry, so you never have to probe `/stats` to learn which props a player can settle.

## Versioning and deprecation

Every endpoint lives under a major-version URL path prefix (`/v1/…`). Changes within a major version are additive only (new endpoints, optional parameters, response fields, competitions, stat keys, error codes); clients must ignore unknown fields. Breaking changes ship as a new major path (`/v2/…`) served alongside the old one. Documented exception: the 2026-09-11 paid self-serve quota hard-stop changed at-cap metered `/v1` responses from `200` to `429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED` without a new major path; see the changelog. Deprecations are announced with `Deprecation` (RFC 9745) and `Sunset` (RFC 8594) response headers on the affected operation, `deprecated: true` in this document, and a dated changelog entry — at least 90 days before sunset for an operation and 12 months for a whole major version. Full policy: https://statshawk.ai/docs/getting-started/versioning

## Permissions and scopes

The REST API is read-only: an API key can read data and consume quota, never write data or manage the account. Keys come in two environments, `sk_live_…` and `sk_test_…`, so traffic classes can be rotated and audited independently; create one key per integration. All plans include every endpoint, including `/v1/analysis/*`. The MCP server uses OAuth 2.1 scopes `stats:read` and `analysis:read`. Details: https://statshawk.ai/docs/getting-started/permissions

## Rate limits and errors

Every metered response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (per-second GCRA limiter, per account); monthly quota is reported in `X-Account-Quota-*`. A `429` carries `Retry-After` and an `error.code` of `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` or `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`. All errors share the typed `ErrorResponse` shape `{"error": {"code", "message"}}` and every response carries `X-Request-Id`. Rate limits: https://statshawk.ai/docs/getting-started/rate-limits · Error codes: https://statshawk.ai/docs/getting-started/error-codes
